proposal.title: Campaign timeline — Team Edition: whole-team development
proposal.reason: Convert this campaign to an independent dated timeline object. Dates are resolved from its execution process without changing precision. Preserve all existing event/subprocess ownership; marketing-step reference_id is absent throughout. Consolidate presentations, campaign material and useful claim-policy requirements into narrated steps; remove historical acceptance labels and duplicate import fragments. Product-owned launch links remain authoritative and validated through the explicit transitional execution mapping. Add the campaign alongside the unchanged execution-process step in process.team_edition_server_development.

before.title: Team Edition: whole-team development
before.objective: Recruit development teams to Team Edition by demonstrating shared projects, review, reproducible builds and separate CP/M and AIONix targets.
message: campaign message: Complex products. Whole teams. One development environment.
campaign promise: Your team’s development environment should outlast any single computer architecture.
claim_policy: claim policy: Robustness is a design goal demonstrated by recovery and reproducible builds, not an untested most-robust comparison. No write-once/run-anywhere or Apple/Commodore launch claim.

after.title: Team Edition: whole-team development
after.objective: Recruit development teams to Team Edition by demonstrating shared projects, review, reproducible builds and separate CP/M and AIONix targets.
message: Complex products. Whole teams. One development environment.
Your team’s development environment should outlast any single computer architecture.

marketing_presentation.description: Prepare campaign demonstrations, dealer materials and press briefings that explain whole-team development, hardware/storage requirements, C source portability and separate target binaries.
Robustness is a design goal demonstrated by recovery and reproducible builds, not an untested most-robust comparison. No write-once/run-anywhere or Apple/Commodore launch claim.

marketing_steps.description: Introduce Team Edition at COMDEX on 19 November 1981.

marketing_presentation.description: Recruit development teams to Team Edition by demonstrating shared projects, review, reproducible builds and separate CP/M and AIONix targets.

marketing_steps.description: Prepare the workshop and trade programme starting on 1 December.

marketing_presentation.description: Prepare the workshop, case-study and trade-advertising follow-up launched by the 1 December end milestone; the 90-day programme is not claimed to have finished on that date.

before.title: Team Edition server development and launch
before.description: Develop and qualify Team Edition shared development services, validate reference-site use and coordinate its COMDEX 1981 launch. Begin with engineering on 1 December 1980 and end with the launch campaign on 1 December 1981, when the existing workshop and trade follow-up begins. Retail deployment, the later 90-day follow-up work and Autodesk sponsorship are not treated as completed development activities.

participant.role: Team Edition engineering and reference-site qualification
platform support, programme sponsorship and launch coordination

inputs.description: The Artemis commercial launch establishes the platform for the Team Edition development system.
Existing AIONix and Artemis development facilities provide the operating-system and hardware basis for shared development services.

steps.description: AION Software developed shared projects, source history, branches, reviews and reproducible builds for development teams.
The team tested permissions, interrupted saves, backup recovery and separate CP/M and AIONix builds at reference sites.
Run the 1 September 1981 reference-site pilots for shared projects, permissions, interrupted saves, recovery and separate CP/M/AIONix builds; participants are not assumed paying customers.
Prepare dealers, present Team Edition at COMDEX and begin the existing workshop/trade follow-up through the dedicated launch campaign.

outcomes.description: Team Edition shared services and distinct CP/M/AIONix target builds undergo reference-site qualification and are presented through the launch campaign, with documented deployment and recovery requirements. Retail installations and sponsored Autodesk work remain separately accounted for.
